header.running_head: Being Stern with those who Oppose the Commands of Rasulullaah ﷺ

blocks.text: wear clothes of silk?" "But I wear silk," explained Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA). "Are they at all like you (do they have the same complaint)?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) challenged.[^1]
Tearing the Garments of Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) and Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed (RA)

Hadhrat Ibn Seereen reports that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Waleed (RA) once went to Hadhrat Umar (RA) wearing a silk garment. "What is this, O Khaalid?" enquired Hadhrat Umar (RA). "What is wrong with it, O Ameerul Mu'mineen?" Hadhrat Khaalid (RA) asked, "Does Ibn Auf not wear this?" Hadhrat Umar (RA) replied, "Are you at all like Ibn Auf and do you have the problem he has? In the name of Allaah do I entreat every person in this room to grab hold of that part of the garment closest to him and to tear it until nothing is left of it."[^2]

The narration has already passed in the chapter entitled "The Sahabah (RA) Place Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Ahead for Khilaafah"[^3] that Hadhrat Khaalid bin Sa'eed bin Aas (RA) was in Yemen when Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away. He arrived in Madinah a month after Rasulullaah ﷺ's demise wearing a silken cloak. When he met Hadhrat Umar (RA) and Hadhrat Ali (RA), Hadhrat Umar (RA) called out to the people, "Tear up his cloak! How can he wear silk when he is a Muslim man in times of peace?" The people then tore his cloak up.[^4]
Hadhrat Umar (RA) Cuts Off Silk Buttons from a Garment

Hadhrat Abdah bin Abu Lubaabah reports that he was informed that Hadhrat Umar (RA) once passed a person in the Masjid. The man was performing salaah and wearing a green garment that had buttons of silk. Standing by his side, Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Lengthen your salaah as much as you please but I shall remain here until you complete." When he saw that the man had turned towards him (after completing the salaah), Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Show me your garment." Hadhrat Umar (RA) then took the garment and cut off all the silk buttons before giving it back to the man.[^5]
